Drop the grid cells that hold no value at any time step

Source: R/copernicus.R
drop_never_observed.Rd

The readers keep cells that are empty at a time step, so that a cloud gap arrives as an NA that fill_satellite_gaps() can fill. A cell that is empty at every time step of the request is a different case: land, or outside the product's domain. Those are dropped, as they always were, because matchData() joins each observation to the nearest cell. Kept, an observation on the coast would join to the land cell beside it and take its NA instead of the nearest value at sea.

Usage

drop_never_observed(covars, value_columns)

Arguments

covars

a data frame of x, y, value columns and time columns

value_columns

the value columns

Value

covars without the cells that never hold a value

Details

The two cannot be told apart from the data alone when a cell is clouded at every requested time step, as it may be on a one-date request. Such a cell is dropped like land, which is how every cloud gap was treated before.
